correctness.rationale: In characteristic two the diagonal Rota–Baxter identity forces every operator output to square to zero, including each value of a local map. With independent nonzero natural-basis squares, the square-zero set is exactly the annihilator; maps into it satisfy the full identity. In the remaining two-dimensional rank-one case over an even finite field, multiplication is xy=B(x,y)v with B nondegenerate and the square-zero space is a line Ku. Every candidate is R(x)=ℓ(x)u. The full identity becomes ℓ(v)(ℓ(x)B(u,y)+ℓ(y)B(u,x))=0, giving the union of two functional lines. They coincide exactly when v²=0, then forcing every local map to vanish at v. Otherwise the two evaluation kernels intersect only at zero, giving every possible square-zero value at each nonzero input and hence all q² local maps. The first three cases are annihilator cases. Counting labeled rank-one nonzero square pairs on each projective line gives q−1 isotropic pairs on each of q−1 nonaxis lines, none on the axes; the other three census entries follow from zero, one-zero and invertible square matrices. Independent exhaustive binary testing of all 16 algebras and 16 maps per algebra (all input pairs for ordinary operators and all inputs for local witnesses) gave census (1,6,6,1,2) and per-table count pairs (16,16), (4,4), (1,1), (2,2), (3,4). The included verify.py, inspected but not executed, gives wider finite replay cases; no finite test substitutes for the symbolic argument. Rigidity is valid over arbitrary characteristic-two fields; the complete counts, which use square roots, are stated for finite fields only.

value.rationale: The smallest dimension admitting separation has a complete intrinsic test: zero annihilator, one-dimensional E² and a nonsquare-zero generator of E². The two distinct lines of ordinary operators realize every allowed value pointwise despite not filling the linear map space. This supplies both a mechanism and exact gap, not an arbitrary sample or a table of isomorphism classes. The labeled census measures how often the mechanism occurs among all natural-basis tables.
